Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: cvdFacilityCounty
candidates.comment: A geographical identification relation between a CDCPMD record and the county of the NHSN facility it applies to. Also called: facility county, hospital county, reporting county. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvd facility county "Los Angeles County", "NHSN Record" cvd facility county "Cook County", "Hospital Report" cvd facility county "King County". Distinct from cvdFacilityId, which is the identifier of the facility.

candidates.label: cvdNumVentUse
candidates.comment: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of mechanical ventilators currently in use. Also called: ventilators in use, occupied ventilators, ventilator usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num vent use "70", "Facility B Report" cvd num vent use "30", "Medical Center C" cvd num vent use "150". Distinct from cvdNumVent, which is the total number of ventilators available.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: actionPlatform
candidates.comment: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system. Examples: "A web application's action platform is 'WebPlatform'.", "A mobile app's action platform is 'iOS'."
